title: Section 5.4 subtracts four columns that are not on one scale, in a section that prints the conversion factor 40 lines later. Put them on a common scale and re-read the comparison.
cost: offline, $0 -- no API, no GPU, no download. Reads M26's records, m26c_pneural_cache.npz, m32_eterna_cache.npz.
why: Section 5.1 states the rule: two readouts on different columns 'are not on one scale and may not simply be subtracted', and it obeys the rule by reporting each column's pooled within-stratum SD and testing the standardised difference on one design-clustered resample.

Section 5.4 breaks that rule. Its table holds the matched contrast in the measured rescue factor (+0.0539) beside the matched contrast in each predictor's own pair probability (+0.0605, -0.0304, -0.00569), and it subtracts across them: 'The measurement is indistinguishable from the transformer (-0.00662)'. That subtraction carries the word 'tracking' in Claim 2 and in the abstract.

The same section then prints the conversion factor. Its upper-bound paragraph multiplies each predictor's contrast by that predictor's within-stratum slope on the outcome (+0.12059, +0.20692) and divides by the measured contrast, giving 6.8% and 23.2%. 0.0605 x 0.20692 / 0.0539 = 0.2323, so the arithmetic is the paper's own.

So the section knows the probability column must be multiplied by a slope before it can enter rescue units, uses that fact to compute a bound, and forty lines earlier subtracts the unmultiplied number.

algebraic_bridge_established_before_the_.note: Verified symbolically and numerically before this declaration was written, so the run tests it rather than discovers it.
algebraic_bridge_established_before_the_.identity: bound = Delta_p * g / alpha_R = rho * (Delta_p/SD_p) / (alpha_R/SD_R), because g = rho * SD_R / SD_p
algebraic_bridge_established_before_the_.consequence: the slope route is the SD route attenuated by rho. The two routes answer different questions -- 'does the predictor separate the pair types as sharply, each in its own units' versus 'how much of the measured effect could travel through this predictor' -- and neither is a correction of the other. What is not either question is the raw subtraction.

arms.A1: pooled within-stratum SD of each of the four columns on the matched set
arms.A2: each column's matched contrast divided by its own within-stratum SD, with a target-clustered 95% interval
arms.A3: paired differences of the SD-standardised contrasts, measurement minus each predictor, all four columns evaluated inside the SAME resample draw
arms.A4: slope route: each predictor's contrast multiplied by its own within-stratum slope on the outcome, differenced against the measured contrast, with the slope RESAMPLED inside the same draw rather than held as a constant
arms.A5: numerical check of the bridge identity on the point estimates
arms.A6: reverse control -- reproduce the four published contrasts, the three published raw paired differences, and the two published bounds

verification_before_any_arm_is_read.V1_zero_point: a column standardised against itself gives a paired difference of exactly 0 in every draw; a constant column has SD 0 and must be refused rather than divided by
verification_before_any_arm_is_read.V2_equivalent_form: the standardised contrast computed as (contrast / SD) must equal the contrast recomputed after the column itself is standardised, to 1e-9, in every draw
verification_before_any_arm_is_read.V3_reverse_control: the four raw contrasts must reproduce the manuscript's published values to 1e-4, and the raw paired difference measurement-minus-transformer must reproduce -0.00662 to 1e-4, before any standardised number is read
verification_before_any_arm_is_read.V4_bridge: the identity above must hold to 1e-9 on the point estimates for both predictors that have a published bound

kill_conditions.K1: if A6 fails to reproduce any published contrast or the published raw difference to 1e-4, VOID -- the estimator is not the paper's
kill_conditions.K2: if V1, V2 or V4 fails, VOID
kill_conditions.K3: if any column's pooled within-stratum SD is below 0.01, that column is reported WITHOUT a standardised value rather than divided by a number too small to be stable
kill_conditions.K4: if the two routes disagree in SIGN on the same comparison, neither is reported as the answer and both are reported as the finding

staked_predictions.text: the paired interval on the SD-standardised measurement-minus-transformer difference EXCLUDES zero, so the word 'indistinguishable' does not survive standardisation
the slope-route difference between the measured contrast and the transformer's contrast converted into rescue units EXCLUDES zero
the SD-standardised measurement-minus-transformer difference is POSITIVE, i.e. the measurement separates the pair types more sharply in its own units than the transformer does in its own

wording_rules_binding_on_the_manuscript.W1: a difference between two columns in raw units may not be printed as licensing a conclusion. The raw paired differences are either removed or kept with an explicit statement, at the number, that they are not on one scale.
wording_rules_binding_on_the_manuscript.W2: the word 'tracking' in Claim 2 and in the abstract must be restated in whichever unit this run supports, or withdrawn. It may not be left as it is.
wording_rules_binding_on_the_manuscript.W3: the manuscript must state that the two routes answer different questions and give the bridge identity, rather than presenting either as a correction of the other.
wording_rules_binding_on_the_manuscript.W4: differences BETWEEN predictors (transformer minus thermodynamic, and the two nearest-neighbour models against each other) are within one unit system and are NOT affected by this run. The decomposition and training-data axes of Claim 2 stand unless this run says otherwise.
